summary: Al/InAsOI Josephson junctions exhibit exceptionally weak electron-phonon coupling with $\Sigma \approx (3$-$4) \times 10^7$ W/(m$^3$K$^n$) and $n \approx 5.8$ at sub-Kelvin temperatures, enabling strong thermal decoupling while maintaining high-quality superconductivity with $T_c \approx 1.2$ K. The platform combines transparent S-Sc interfaces, full electrostatic tunability, and a noise-equivalent temperature of 100-200 μK/Hz for Josephson thermometry, making it suitable for coherent caloritronics and gate-controlled thermal circuits.
motivation: Coherent caloritronics requires weak electron-phonon coupling, but this is difficult to combine with high-quality superconducting proximity effects; InAsOI was designed to provide both transparent superconducting contacts and intrinsically weak thermal relaxation.
method: Josephson junction thermometry was used to extract electronic temperature $T_e$ under Joule heating at various bath temperatures, fitting the power-law relation $T_e = (\dot{Q}_{\mathrm{inj}}/(\Sigma V) + T^n)^{1/n}$ between 100-220 mK to determine the e-ph coupling parameters $\Sigma$ and $n$.
result: InAsOI shows $\Sigma$ values 1-2 orders of magnitude smaller than typical metals and comparable to or superior to other semiconductor platforms, with stability in $\Sigma$ and $n$ over a 120 mK temperature range and fits with reduced $\chi^2 \approx 1.1 \times 10^{-4}$.
